record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Find an explicit fast-growing integer sequence a(n), meaning log a(n) / log n → ∞, that is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence both for powers of a single transformation and for arbitrary commuting transformations.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Give an explicit example of a fast growing sequence that is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers and commuting transformations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space.

(i) A sequence of positive integers $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is called good for multiple recurrence of powers of a single transformation if for every invertible measure-preserving transformation $T:X\to X$, every integer $k\ge 1$, and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{-a(n)}A\cap T^{-2a(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-k a(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$

(ii) The sequence $(a(n))$ is called good for multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation if for every such system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, every $k\ge 1$, and all $f_1,\dots,f_k\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T^{a(n)}x)\, f_2(T^{2a(n)}x)\cdots f_k(T^{k a(n)}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

(iii) The sequence $(a(n))$ is called good for multiple recurrence of commuting transformations if for every $k\ge 1$, every collection $T_1,\dots,T_k$ of commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{-a(n)}A\cap T_2^{-a(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_k^{-a(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$

(iv) The sequence $(a(n))$ is called good for multiple convergence of commuting transformations if, in the same setup, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T_1^{a(n)}x)\, f_2(T_2^{a(n)}x)\cdots f_k(T_k^{a(n)}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ for all $f_1,\dots,f_k\in L^\infty(\mu)$.

(v) A sequence of positive integers $(a(n))$ is called fast growing if
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log a(n)}{\log n}=+\infty,$$
i.e., $a(n)$ grows faster than any polynomial in $n$.

Problem. Exhibit an explicit fast-growing integer sequence $(a(n))$ that is simultaneously good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence in both senses (i)–(ii) (powers of a single transformation) and (iii)–(iv) (commuting transformations).
artifact.status_search_result: No explicit construction satisfying all four properties simultaneously was found in the literature search. Known good sequences for multiple recurrence/convergence are typically of polynomial growth (integer polynomials, Hardy field functions of polynomial growth), or involve random/non-explicit constructions. The problem appears to remain open as of recent surveys and papers on multiple ergodic averages.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence and convergence for Hardy sequences of polynomial growth
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiple recurrence and convergence for Hardy sequences of polynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: Established results concern polynomial-growth sequences, not fast-growing ones.

status_evidence.title: Random sequences and pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: Random (non-explicit) constructions of sequences good for multiple convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Known fast-growing sequences good for multiple recurrence/convergence are typically random and not explicit.

status_evidence.title: Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence and recurrence results for Hardy field functions, which are of polynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances do not provide explicit fast-growing sequences answering the problem.
